subject: mathematics
question_text: If a cos2θ + b sin2θ = c has θ₁, θ₂ as its solutions, then show that (i) tanθ₁ + tanθ₂ = 2b/(c+a), (ii) tanθ₁ · tanθ₂ = (c−a)/(c+a), and hence show that tan(θ₁+θ₂) = b/a.

mark_split.label: Read off the sum of roots
Read off the product and finish

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — name each move in order, and say which general solution formula you would use.

steps.label: Form a quadratic in tanθ
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. Substitute the tangent forms of cos2θ and sin2θ, clear the denominator, and collect. What comes out is a quadratic in tanθ — which is the whole idea.
lines: Given a cos2θ + b sin2θ = c
⇒ a − a tan²θ + 2b tanθ = c + c tan²θ

recall.must_convey: That the tangent forms of cos2θ and sin2θ are substituted and the equation collected into the quadratic (c+a)tan²θ − 2b tanθ + (c−a) = 0.
accept: substitute the tan forms of cos two theta and sin two theta then clear the denominator and collect into a quadratic in tan theta
turn it into c plus a tan squared minus two b tan plus c minus a equals zero
use the half angle tangent substitutions to get a quadratic
cos two theta and sin two theta ni tan lo rasi quadratic ga marchali
form a quadratic equation in tan theta

steps.why: θ₁ and θ₂ are the two solutions, so tanθ₁ and tanθ₂ are the two ROOTS of this quadratic. That is what makes the sum and product available without solving anything.
common_mistakes: Trying to solve the original equation for θ.
Sign slip when moving the c terms across.

steps.label: Read off the sum of roots
steps.margin_note: Third mark. For ax² + bx + c = 0 the sum of the roots is −b/a. Here that is −(−2b)/(c+a), which is 2b/(c+a).
lines: This is a quadratic in tanθ with roots tanθ₁, tanθ₂.
Sum of the roots of Ax² + Bx + C = 0 is −B/A:

recall.must_convey: That the sum of the roots is −B/A = 2b/(c+a).
accept: the sum of the roots is minus B over A which gives two b over c plus a
sum of roots formula gives two b by c plus a
tan theta one plus tan theta two is two b over c plus a
sum of roots minus B by A, two b by c plus a vasthundi
read the sum off the coefficients
heard_as: two b over c plus a

steps.why: The two minus signs cancel: the coefficient of tanθ is −2b, and the formula puts a minus in front of it. Missing one of them flips the sign.

steps.label: Read off the product and finish
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The product is C/A. Then tan(θ₁+θ₂) uses the compound formula, and the (c+a) cancels top and bottom, leaving b/a.
lines: Product of the roots is C/A:

recall.must_convey: That the product of roots is (c−a)/(c+a), and that tan(θ₁+θ₂) simplifies to b/a.
accept: the product is C over A which is c minus a over c plus a then the compound formula gives two b over two a which is b over a
product of roots then tan of the sum simplifies to b over a
the c plus a cancels leaving b over a
product c minus a by c plus a, tarvata tan sum formula tho b by a vasthundi

steps.why: The denominator 1 − (c−a)/(c+a) becomes ((c+a) − (c−a))/(c+a) = 2a/(c+a). Both fractions share (c+a), so it cancels — which is why the answer is so simple.
common_mistakes: Failing to put the 1 over a common denominator.
Cancelling before combining, and losing the 2a.
